Maintenance Report — MNT-0126-002

Asset: WELL-0126 (NE-07 Well 126, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 28 Mar 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 570 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0126-0004 on 2023-03-02 Report written: 30 Mar 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0126-0004 showed the wellhead at 10.7 °C with the air at 8.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 285 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 228 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0126-002 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0126-010

Asset: WELL-0126 (NE-07 Well 126, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 06 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 10 Apr 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 92 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0126-0061 on 2024-04-04 Report written: 11 Apr 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0126-0061 showed the wellhead at 26.6 °C with the air at 22.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 2 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.
